## What Is Glaido?

Glaido AI dictation app — 

Glaido positions itself as "the voice layer for every app" and "the world's fastest dictation" — the latter is a marketing claim with no published independent benchmark.

Glaido swaps your keyboard for your voice. Hold a hotkey, talk, and it drops the text wherever your cursor sits. It calls itself "the voice layer for every app" and claims "the world's fastest dictation."

### Who makes Glaido

At launch, Glaido looked like a one-person side project with no company behind it. Not anymore. [...] ### Glaido fits you if you

 Dictate occasionally and want a polished free tier — 2,000 words a week with Agent Mode covers a lot of light use, no card needed.
 Use a Mac or Windows PC, are fine with cloud processing, and just want dictation that works across every app.
 Want AI formatting and an agent layer without configuring anything.
 Are in the EU and value Glaido's explicit GDPR posture.

### Choose Voibe instead if you [...] System-wide dictation. One hotkey types into any app.
 AI auto-edits. It punctuates, capitalizes, and strips filler on its own — you don't dictate the commas.
 Agent Mode. Glaido's AI-workflow layer, now free (it used to be Pro-only). The docs are thin on what it actually does, so treat it as promising, not proven.
 Custom dictionary and prompts. Add your names and jargon, and steer the output style.
 100 languages.
 Prioritized processing (Pro). Faster queue, early features.
 Team features (Enterprise). SSO, SAML, dedicated processing, API access.

None of this is unique to Glaido — AI cleanup, custom vocabulary, and multilingual support are standard in 2026. But the bundle hangs together, and putting Agent Mode in the free tier is a generous call.

Hold a hotkey, speak, and it pastes cleaned-up text into whatever field has focus: Slack, Gmail, Notion, Cursor, or a browser tab. A separate command hotkey sends spoken requests to an AI model instead, so you can rewrite selected text or ask for a web search without leaving the app you are in. [...] ### Early complaints

results.content:
## Built to stay out of your way

Glaido runs as a lightweight native Mac app. No browser tab, no Electron wrapper, and no startup friction. Press a keyboard shortcut, speak, and your words appear where you're already working.

It's designed to feel immediate, so your thoughts stay in flow. Glaido adapts output to your writing context and keeps punctuation, structure, and tone aligned with the work in front of you.

Most importantly, it works reliably across the apps you use every day, so voice can become a true default input method instead of a novelty.

## Who it's for

Glaido is built for people who write a lot and want to write faster without sacrificing quality: [...] Log inDownload

# Introducing Glaido

Meet Glaido, the voice dictation tool that actually understands what you're writing. Context-aware, real-time, and built for professionals on Mac.

Glaido team,

## Writing is slow. Talking is fast.

The gap between them has always been frustrating. Traditional dictation tools turn your voice into text, and that's about it. They don't know if you're writing an email, a Slack message, or a code comment. They don't adjust formatting. They don't understand punctuation in context.

The result? A wall of unformatted text that takes almost as long to clean up as it would have taken to type.

> We built Glaido to close that gap for good.

## What makes Glaido different [...] ## What makes Glaido different

Glaido is voice dictation that understands context. When you start speaking, Glaido looks at three things:

1. The app you're in (email client, Slack, VS Code, Google Docs, etc.)
2. The text around your cursor (what you've already written)
3. The type of content you're producing (professional email vs. quick reply vs. technical docs)

Then it formats your words to match.

Drafting a professional email? Glaido capitalizes sentences, adds paragraph breaks, and keeps the tone polished. Writing a quick Slack reply? It stays casual and concise. Leaving a code review comment? It formats `inline code references` and keeps technical terms intact.

There is no post-processing step. It happens in real time, as you speak.

## Built to stay out of your way
